Benham propone leer primero el carácter: Benham suggests first reading the character of each line: the more even, clear, and deep it is, and the less broken, crossed, or marked with islands, the better what it represents is expressed. A wide, shallow line is read as scattered energy that is hard to turn into results. If one line is noticeably deeper than the others, what it represents is your strongest point; if it is the weakest, it is the point to look after. According to Benham, vertical lines favor the flow of energy, and horizontal lines that cross them interrupt it; an irregular line is read from beginning to end, because the thin and deep stretches correspond to stages of different effort. He makes clear that lines change with time and experience, so they are a map of tendencies, not a verdict.
Para Cheiro, la línea del corazón debe s: For Cheiro, the heart line should be clear and well marked. If it starts under Jupiter (the index finger), it speaks of idealistic, loyal affection; if it starts under Saturn (the middle finger), of more passionate and less demonstrative affection; if it starts between the two, of a calmer, more serene nature in love. A pale line without branches is associated with restrained affection, and a line with many little marks, with inconstancy in relationships. A curved line is usually associated with expressiveness. Benham observes that in most hands the heart line starts deep and ends wider and more shallow, because in the first twenty years the heart acts with more force and over time one tends to love with more caution. These are symbolic nuances, not a judgment on how you love.
La línea de la cabeza representa tradici: The head line traditionally represents your style of thinking: how ideas are organized, how decisions are made, and what place analysis, creativity, and intuition have. It does not measure intelligence, memory, education, or professional ability.

Cheiro warns that its importance depends on the type of hand: it is less significant on elementary or spatulate hands than on square, philosophic, conic, or psychic hands, and even so a short, clear line on a square hand weighs more than a long one on a conic hand. When it appears visible, it can be read as a sense of purpose or of direction toward certain goals. When it can’t be made out, tradition usually speaks of a more flexible path, built through several decisions and opportunities, not a lack of destiny. An irregular course is interpreted as possible changes of stage or priorities.
